newsitem.title: ITALY: Italians overwhelmingly oppose secession - poll.
newsitem.headline: Italians overwhelmingly oppose secession - poll.

text.p: An opinion poll published on Friday as separatist Umberto Bossi prepared to proclaim a breakaway "republic" in northern Italy found 85.6 percent of Italians were against secession.

But the survey by the Datamedia institute showed strong support for a federal Italy and substantial understanding for the popular discontent that underpins the secessionist campaign by Bossi and his Northern League.
Bossi, whose party won 3.7 million votes in the north at Italy's last election in April, was embarking on Friday on a three-day "March to the Sea" along the River Po to Venice.
He intends to proclaim a "federal republic of Padania" there on Sunday as a first step to what he says will be full independence within a year for Italy's affluent north .

Datamedia, which conducted the survey among 1,002 Italians on Thursday, said only 7.6 percent of respondents were in favour of secession. Those against were 85.6 percent with the rest "don't knows" or non-replies.
A narrow majority, 52.9 percent, said they believed a federal Italy was the right way to proceed and 41.6 percent said they considered northern discontent well-founded.
Datamedia gave no indication of the geographical breakdown of the poll.
Bossi's party built its following on northern frustration with high taxes, suffocating bureaucracy and the corruption that brought down Italy's old political class four years ago.
It has switched to a secessionist from a federalist agenda since the last election, when Bossi failed in his bid to secure the balance of power in the national parliament.
The centre-left government and the main opposition say they are committed to federal reform, though the process will require changes to the constitution expected to take at least two years.
Bossi's latest challenge has led to calls from some politicians for parliament to move faster towards federalism.
